data.content:
Here's the complete project. Three files do all the work:

**Program.cs** — wires up the MCP server with HTTP (Streamable HTTP) transport:

**Key points:**

| Concept | How |
|---|---|
| **HTTP transport** | `.WithHttpTransport()` + `app.MapMcp()` — uses Streamable HTTP (SSE) at the root `/` endpoint |
| **Resources** | Mark class with `[McpServerResourceType]`, methods with `[McpServerResource]`. Use `UriTemplate` with `{param}` placeholders for parameterized resources |
| **Tools** | Mark class with `[McpServerToolType]`, methods with `[McpServerTool]` + `[Description]` |
| **Registration** | `.WithToolsFromAssembly()` / `.WithResourcesFromAssembly()` auto-discovers everything |

The resource attribute uses **`Title`** (not `Description`) for the human-readable label. The server returns a `Mcp-Session-Id` header for session management. NuGet packages needed: `ModelContextProtocol` and `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore`.
